In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surat al-Takathur

It is Meccan.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase diverts you﴾. That is: the competition for more (wealth) in property and children has preoccupied you from what you were commanded.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 102, verse 2:

And His saying: ﴿Until you visit the graves﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first: "until you die." The second opinion: two clans of Quraysh boasted against each other, namely Banu 'Abd Manaf and Banu al-Zuhra. It was also said: Banu Zuhra and Banu Jumah, and this is the more sound view. They counted the living, and Banu Zuhra outnumbered them; then they counted the dead, and Banu Jumah outnumbered them. This is the meaning of His exalted saying: ﴿Until you visit the graves﴾, that is: you counted those who are in the graves.

Shu'bah narrated from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir, from his father, who said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was reciting: 'Your abundance of worldly things has diverted you [from Allah].' He said: 'The son of Adam says: "My wealth, my wealth." And is there anything of your wealth yours except what you have eaten and used up, or worn and worn out, or given in charity and sent ahead?'"

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: This hadith was related to us by Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Sarifini, known as Ibn Hizarmard; Abu al-Qasim ibn Habbabah related to us; al-Baghawi related to us; 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd related to us, from Shu'bah... the hadith. Muslim recorded it from Bundar, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on Surah 102, verse 3:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿No! You are going to know.﴾ It is a threat and a warning.

Verse: "Then, no! You are going to know."

And His saying: ﴿Then no! You are going to know﴾ is a threat following a threat, and a warning following a warning. The meaning is: you will come to know the outcome of your boasting and your competing for abundance when death comes upon you.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, if you knew with certain knowledge﴾. Its response (jawab) is omitted, and the meaning is: Nay, if you knew with certain knowledge, you would have refrained from what you are doing. It is said: [the response is] "What distracted you is the rivalry in worldly increase."

"And His saying: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.﴾ Some of them said: The second is an emphasis of the first, and the meaning in both is one. And some of them said: "You will surely see the Hellfire" from a distance when it is brought forth; then "you will surely see it with the eye of certainty" when you have entered it.

And from Qatadah, he said: "We used to discuss that the knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqin) is to know that Allah will resurrect him after death."

And it is said: "You will surely see the Hellfire" in the grave, and "then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty" on the Day of Resurrection."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 102, verse 8:

And His saying: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (al-na'im).﴾ Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas: "The pleasure (al-na'im) is the soundness of the bodies, hearing and sight. Allah the Exalted will ask His servants on the Day of Resurrection how they used them, although He knows best about that from them."

And from Ibn Mas'ud: that it is security and health.

And from Qatada: it is the wholesome food and the refreshing drink.

Abu Hurayrah related, traced back to the Prophet: "It is the cool shade and the cold water."

'Umar ibn Abi Salama related that the Prophet, Abu Bakr and 'Umar came to the home of Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayhan, and they ate meat and dates there. Then the Prophet said: "This is from the pleasure about which you will be asked."

It is related that 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be asked about this?" He said: "Yes, except a morsel with which a man repels his hunger, a garment with which he covers his nakedness, and a dwelling into which he enters to protect himself from heat and cold."

Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid who said: "All the pleasures of this world."

And from some of them: sleep together with well-being.

Abu 'Isa (al-Tirmidhi) mentioned reports on this, among them what we have related from the hadith of Mutarrif, and he said: "It is a hasan sahih hadith." Among them is the hadith of al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from 'Ali who said: "We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave until ﴿The mutual rivalry in worldly gain diverts you﴾ was revealed."

Abu 'Isa said: "It is a gharib hadith."

Among them is the hadith of Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, from his father who said: "When ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure﴾ was revealed, al-Zubayr said: 'O Messenger of Allah, about which pleasure will we be asked, when they are only the two blacks: the dates and the water?' He said: 'Indeed, that will come to pass.'" He said: "It is a hasan hadith."

It is related from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayrah who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure﴾, the people said: 'O Messenger of Allah, about which pleasure will we be asked, when they are only the two blacks, while the enemy is present and our swords are on our shoulders?' He said: 'Indeed, that will come to pass.'"

It is related from al-Dahhak ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Azram al-Ash'ari who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah said: "The first thing a servant will be asked about on the Day of Resurrection concerning pleasure is that it will be said to him: 'Did We not make your body healthy and give you to drink of cold water?'"

He said: "It is a gharib hadith, and Allah knows best."
